title: Input and output: byte and character streams

videos.script: The last part of the course is the standard library, and it starts with the oldest piece: reading and writing. {{bytes}} A file is bytes. Text is characters. Between the two sits an encoding, and when the writer and the reader disagree about it, Sertão comes back as something nobody wrote. {{buffer}} Then speed. Reading a file one byte at a time asks the operating system for every byte. A buffer asks once for thousands, and the same file is read twelve times faster. {{close}} Then the resource every stream holds: a file handle. Forget to close it, and after a few dozen files the operating system says no more. {{std}} And last, the three streams every program already has, standard in, out and error, and how a Java program becomes one step in a pipe.
